summary: One TLS handshake presents one server certificate. The unverified S2 attempt must end; enrollment is server-side and policy-driven, never during a pending connection; S6 is a new connection attempt whose channel turns green.

Each request is consumed at its destination CA and never reappears. The subordinate-CA request in the flashback carries a CA=true band and a must-read 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' tag, so it cannot read as the RDP request being forwarded to the root.
The root's self-signed seal is revealed as an existing property, not animated closed; the root performs no operation in the present.
The handshake proof has its own shape (a signature impression), distinct from every key and included in the C-11 silhouette checks.
The trust-store recall does not travel (transport none, era recall); it is a shimmer on the card already in the cradle.
B-04.1's text says the capsule pauses at the server's outbound port, framed with the AD node; it never goes to AD.
The model and the notes agree on the self-signed certificate's contents (subject CN; no SAN modelled).
The notes state that the template definition is read from the AD enrollment policy before key generation; B-04.1 is the CA-selection lookup.
hard_test: none (documentation-only; not expressible as a model test)

summary: Each server receives a copy of its issuing CA certificate with the enrollment response (Intermediate store) before it presents it; the copy is distinct from the CA's crown certificate.
Certificates are presented only after the connection pulse arrives; each revocation tick starts only after all CRL fetches for that chain have landed.
The client verifies each handshake proof against the server certificate's public key; the proof ends its life there, before the session is established.
Wording: the root issues and signs the CA certificate from the request; a CA never 'signs the request' (spec, glossary, notes, model summary aligned).
Issuing CA 2's certificate already exists (dimmed on its crown from B-07.3); B-08.3 is a reveal sweep; the root's key module and press stay dark in B-08.3 and B-09.2.

Notes state that this lab configuration would usually satisfy server authentication by Kerberos; 'Unverified' means the certificate cannot be validated through the PKI; no named setting is claimed for 'policy requires a trusted certificate'.
Docs-only browser caveat: online revocation checking depends on the browser and policy; the film depicts a client configured to check CDP/CRL per link.
The undeployed Online Responder has no host; the 'OCSP if deployed' tag sits on the client's revocation check slot, not the kiosk.
The pki.malawi.lab kiosk is only passively highlighted as where a fetch could go; nothing is requested or answers.
Each server's intermediate is a distinct object (copy_of the CA's certificate, held in its Intermediate store); the CA's own crown certificate never moves.
Glossary: a standalone CA does not require AD and does not use templates.
No generic 'trusted CA'; use 'a CA that chains to a trusted root'.
The proof-of-possession seal stays on the capsule until the capsule is consumed; nothing ring-shaped remains at the server.
During the lookup the capsule is held at the RDP server's own outbound port, clearly apart from AD; the query pulse is the event.
All four CA checks and the S8 restriction note are readable, unoccluded and on separate lines while they resolve.
No present-tense check list or check slot appears in the flashback.
Issuer links are trust-link light, gold at the root blending into the CA colour; never a white wire.
The key pulse in the closed container and the handshake proof's arrival and verification are readable at film scale in S6 and S9.
The client side shows the FQDN being connected to.
The issued card shows a validity bar and small AIA/CDP ports.
Issuing CA 1 dims to the ineligible grey during eligibility.
The CA=true band and the sealing by Issuing CA 1's module are readable.
Two CRL fetches are visible before the browser revocation tick.
'Trusted RDP connection established' holds only after the channel has turned green.
No label plane ever fills the frame or sits near the lens.
Trust links are curved, gradient light that grows when introduced and settles; no static straight connectors.
Issuer links carry gold-to-CA colour; the ineligible CA is grey.
Check lists and tags are compact and stand beside the focal subject, not across it.
No speckle on captions or plates; noise restrained.
Focal subjects of B-02.2, B-06.1 and B-06.5 are framed large enough to read.
hard_test: none (framing; planned-film C-03 audit plus discriminator re-check)

summary: Host labels and template badges never overprint each other.
No label is cropped by the frame edge or outside title-safe.
Captions never cover the focal action.
Camera moves are eased and never enter label space or clip geometry.
hard_test: planned-film camera audit (tools motion) plus discriminator re-check

summary: No unidentifiable key-like shape stays outside a container after the capsule leaves.
Focal subjects have a visible key and rim; less emissive wash.
Wide shots have a background layer; no void with a finite floor edge.
The flashback tag 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' is readable for its hold.
No live check text in the flashback.
The proof-of-possession beam is a soft tapering light, not a rod.
Every required caption renders clean, without speckle or ghosting.
Key states are unambiguous: the private key visibly locks into its container, and the public key has no key silhouette.
Captions >= 30 px and must-read labels >= 18 px cap height at 1080p, measured from the glyphs.
The four CA checks are an unoccluded column, clear of nameplate, capsule and module.
SAN and EKU are readable while the card is the focal subject.
The validation checks face the camera, sit inside title-safe at one size and do not cover the chain.
AIA tags stand to one side of the chain, inside title-safe.
Host, site, badge, CA 2 and eligibility plates never overlap each other or leave the frame.
Every visible label's bounds stay inside title-safe.
The Root CA name sits on a dark plate, unoccluded, at a readable size.
Both flashback tags are readable and isolated on plates.
No caption plate intersects the focal subject's projected bounds.
The packet carries the role-colour CIEDE2000 and CVD results.
'Self-signed' and 'Unverified' do not overlap; the server plate leaves the badge text clear.
Caption plates are solid; nothing shows through them.
